task.description: Hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b) — validate CODE-DESIGNER output for PIN-03, PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01 (handoff wf02-batch-5-20260812-01-code-designer, result.status=PARTIAL). Read all four design artefacts in full, plus docs/requirements.yaml for the real AC text of each requirement, plus src/engine/pin_resolver.zig, src/engine/instance.zig, src/definition/promotion.zig, src/api/routes/promotion.zig for ground truth on what exists today. Verify: (1) PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01 are complete designs covering every one of their own AC bullets with no unjustified gaps or ambiguity BACKEND-DEV would have to resolve unilaterally. (2) PIN-03s PARTIAL framing is legitimate, not a cop-out: confirm AC3 (DEPRECATED-after-start) genuinely cannot be built against the current service_catalog schema (no version/status column) by checking the schema yourself (migrations/049_repository_service_catalog.sql and any later ALTERs), and confirm the design proposes a real, implementable scoped structural substitute for AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 rather than skipping them too. (3) No implementation code in any artefact; no fenced code block exceeds 40 lines (python3 tools/lint_design_artefact.py already reported 0 findings per CODE-DESIGNER — spot check this claim). (4) Type classification (per templates/lego-catalog.md) is defensible for each requirement. Decide PASS (all four designs — including PIN-03s scoped PARTIAL coverage — are implementation-ready and the scope decision is honestly justified) or FAIL (design is incomplete, ambiguous, contains implementation code, or the PIN-03 scope-down is not actually forced by the schema). This determines whether BACKEND-DEV may proceed.
acceptance_criteria: Every AC of PIN-04/PIN-05/PRM-01 is covered by the design with no ambiguity for BACKEND-DEV
PIN-03 AC3s scope-down is verified against the real service_catalog schema, not taken on faith
No implementation code present in any artefact; fenced code blocks all under 40 lines
Type classification is defensible for each requirement

result.summary: All four design artefacts (PIN-03, PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01) validated as implementation-ready. PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01 cover every AC bullet with no ambiguity BACKEND-DEV would have to resolve unilaterally, no implementation code, all fenced code blocks under the 40-line cap (max 38, in PIN-05). PIN-03 PARTIAL framing is legitimate, not a cop-out: independently confirmed via migrations/049_repository_service_catalog.sql and every later ALTER (GBL-117 adds only scope/owner_tenant_id) that service_catalog has no version/status column, matching ISS-0672/GH-306 which already names PIN-03 AC3 as blocked by the same gap and was filed a batch earlier. PIN-03 proposes a real, testable scoped structural substitute for AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 (execution-time PinMissing guard reusing the existing SERVICE_TASK completion loop, ErrorType taxonomy, and dead-letter routing) and does not skip them. Type E classification is defensible for all four requirements per templates/lego-catalog.md elimination order (Type C/A/D/B ruled out with cited reasons) and its "What stays in Type E" list (engine kernel/replay logic, cross-module orchestration). python tools/lint_design_artefact.py run independently against all four files: 0 findings on each, confirming CODE-DESIGNER claim. Ground truth spot-checked against src/engine/pin_resolver.zig, src/engine/instance.zig, src/engine/service_task.zig, src/engine/reconstruction.zig, src/definition/promotion.zig, src/api/routes/promotion.zig -- every referenced function/pattern (parseConfigFromNodeAttributes, resolveCatalogEndpoint, startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx, CompleteTaskError/FOR UPDATE NOWAIT locking pattern, promoteDefinition/NotATestTenant/ActiveDefinitionNotFound) exists as described. promotion_reviews table confirmed absent from all migrations, supporting PRM-01 Classification rationale section 1 scope boundary.
result.next_action: Route to BACKEND-DEV (Step 2a) for PIN-03 (scoped AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5), PIN-04, PIN-05, PRM-01 implementation
